content.description: Illustration showing removal of rod cap using plastic-faced hammer to tap rod bolts

items.label: (c)
items.text: Using a plastic-faced hammer, tap the rod bolts lightly and lift off the rod cap.

content.text: Keep the bearing inserted with the cap.

content.description: Illustration showing two bearing halves with their inner surfaces visible

items.label: (d)
items.text: Clean the bearings and crankshaft pins.

items.label: (e)
items.text: Inspect each bearing for pitting and radial scratches. If bearings are damaged, replace the bearings.

content.description: Illustration showing laying a strip of plastigage across the crankshaft pin

items.label: (f)
items.text: Lay a strip of plastigage across the crankshaft pin.

content.description: Illustration showing torquing the rod cap nuts with a torque wrench

items.label: (g)
items.text: Align the rod and cap marks and fit on the cap. Torque the rod cap nuts.

content.description: Illustration showing measurement of plastigage clearance at its widest point

items.label: (i)
items.text: Measure the plastigage at its widest point.

content.text: If the clearance is greater than maximum, replace the bearings and/or grind the crank pins.

items.label: (j)
items.text: Clean out any plastigage scraps from the bearing and crankshaft pin.
